messages:
Alex M: Quick sync — noticed a spike in trace query costs when we backfill sampled spans from hot to warm. wondering if retention shape + sampling residue is the real culprit.
Priya K: can you link the dashboard? :mag_right:
Alex M: https://redwood.obsv/d/trace-costs/latest — look at 'query cost per tenant' around 03:00 UTC. big jump after the warm-merge job.
Juan C: oh that warm-merge job materializes span joins which explode cardinality. currently we keep sampled spans with full tags for 7d then compact to keyset.
Sam R: is the compaction step preserving billing keys? if not we might be doing expensive attribute lookups at query time.
Lisa T: correct — compaction strips non-owner attrs, but billing key is in envelope root only for some SDK versions.
Alex M: so two vectors: (1) sampled spans that still have high-cardinality attrs in warm storage, (2) queries that rehydrate attributes by joining against the long index. both costly.
Priya K: tradeoff question: do we shorten sampled-span retention to 24-48h and keep just minimal envelope for 7d? or change compaction to normalize billing attr into a light-weight index?
Juan C: shorter retention reduces immediate query surface but hurts debugging SLOs for customers who inspect older sampled traces.
Sam R: alternative: keep 7d, but run a post-merge normalization that replaces high-cardinality keys with hashed refs and a small lookup table that is cheaper to join.
Lisa T: hashing reduces storage but doesn't help query patterns that do group-by on the original attr. most customer queries do exact-match filters on service+env, not the weird high-cardinality keys.
Alex M: Practically we should measure: incremental cost of joins vs extra cost of maintaining a lookup. Can we prototype a refactor that flips the join direction? e.g., precompute tenant-centric buckets and store a small bloom of keys.
Priya K: +1 to prototype. also need to consider SDKs that send billing keys in span tags vs envelope root. migration pain there.
Juan C: migration option A: backfill normalization during ingest for newer SDKs, option B: runtime fallback lookup. A is cheaper long-term but heavier on ingest CPU.
Sam R: curious about query shape: how many queries actually hit that join path? we should sample N queries and run explain plans.
Alex M: I pulled a query sample — 60% of high-cost queries call our span-attr-join. small set of tenants are responsible for most cost.
Lisa T: maybe a hybrid: for heavy tenants we keep normalized lightweight attrs for 7d; for others we use 48h full-sample + 7d compact. gives a cost isolation knob.
Priya K: that suggests a policy layer: tenant-tier -> sampling retention & compaction strategy. matches product ideas around Dedicated vs Hosted SLAs.
Juan C: Implementation checklist: 1) measure CPU/IO delta for pre-normalize at ingest, 2) prototype hashed-ref lookup table and run query perf, 3) add policy config per tenant.
Sam R: I can run benchmarks for (1) and (2). will need a small dataset and explain plan capture.
observability-bot: Upload complete: warm-merge-job/3490012301/logs.tar.gz (3.2GB).
Alex M: thanks. Sam, aim to have perf numbers by EOD tomorrow. Priya, can you sketch the tenant policy surface? a few toggles like `sample_retention_days`, `compaction_mode` (hash/ref/strip).
Priya K: will do. also will draft migration notes for SDKs — we should add a versioned attr canonicalizer in the ingest path.
Lisa T: one more: cost attribution - if we change compaction semantics we must ensure billing keys survive to cost reports. add regression tests that verify chargeback SKU per sample.
Juan C: agree. test plan: synth tenant with high-card attr; run queries pre/post compaction and compare query time + chargeback correctness.
Sam R: noted. I'll include a few explain snapshots in the PR.
Alex M: OK — next sync Fri. If someone wants to start a short RFC for the prototype, please do and link here. :thumbsup:
Priya K: starting RFC draft now, will ping when ready.
Lisa T: bump if you need data or examples from support — a couple customers already complained about slow historical trace queries.
Alex M: thanks all — thread closed for now, reopen with RFC link.
